parsed.n_justification: Six columns capture the basin's key heterogeneity: (1) lowland urban/developed near Newark, (2) mid-elevation mixed forest in central basin, (3) highland forested headwaters, (4) agricultural/grassland in western portions, (5) wetland/riparian zone, and (6) suburban residential mosaic. columns.description: Lowland urban/developed area near Passaic-Newark, representing impervious-dominated landscape with minimal vegetation
Mid-elevation mixed deciduous forest in central basin, typical of Watchung Mountains
Highland forested headwaters with well-drained soils, representing upper basin conditions
Agricultural/grassland area in western basin with moderately well-drained soils
Great Swamp and riparian wetland zone with poorly-drained hydric soils
Suburban residential mosaic with fragmented forest and lawn vegetation

requires_capabilities: Daily output frequency for seasonal analysis
Partitioned ET components (transpiration, soil evaporation, canopy interception)
Energy balance closure diagnostics (latent heat, sensible heat, net radiation)
Soil moisture and water table depth for water limitation analysis
Vegetation phenology (LAI/SAI) for seasonal vegetation control on ET
assumptions: No local eddy-covariance flux towers exist in the Passaic basin data stack - validation will require alternative approaches (e.g., basin water balance, remote sensing ET products like MODIS MOD16, or regional flux tower networks outside the immediate basin)
NLDAS-2 or CPLHIST forcing provides adequate meteorological drivers for the region (1980-2018 coverage)
Static land cover (year 2000) is acceptable for characterizing climatological ET dynamics, though urbanization trends may affect long-term patterns
Satellite phenology or default PFT parameters adequately represent vegetation seasonality in the absence of site-specific observations
Soil texture classes approximate complex glacial geology and urban soil modifications in the basin
Single-column simulations without lateral flow capture dominant vertical ET processes, though groundwater interactions in the Great Swamp may require PFLOTRAN coupling for full characterization
Spinup of 200 years with accelerated decomposition achieves equilibrium soil carbon and nitrogen pools
Urban and suburban columns may require modified parameters (increased impervious fraction, altered albedo, reduced rooting depth) beyond default PFT settings

Validation strategy will pivot to: (1) comparison with gridded ET products (MODIS, FLUXNET-MTE, SSEBop), (2) water balance closure using USGS streamflow and precipitation, (3) benchmarking against regional flux tower climatologies from similar ecosystems in the Mid-Atlantic region
